robot.name: Figure 03
robot.status_notes: Announced 2025-10-09. Figure says more than 350 units were delivered from BotQ by April 2026 for internal R&D, data collection, housework development and commercial use cases. BMW announced a Figure 03 logistics sequencing use case at Plant Spartanburg in June 2026. No public price, pre-order or home sale was found.

height.notes: Figure product page lists 5'8" (about 173 cm). TIME's launch article describes the robot as 5-foot-6; the official product page value is used here and the conflict is kept in researcher_notes.

weight.notes: Launch post separately says Figure 03 has 9% less mass than Figure 02.

runtime.notes: Product-page figure. During the May 2026 package-sorting livestream, media reported robots rotated out to recharge after roughly 3-4 hours of work.

battery.notes: Battery capacity was not published in reviewed sources. Figure says the pack is certified to UN38.3 and supports 2 kW wireless inductive charging through the feet.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Reported by Humanoid.guide, added 2026-10-29 by automated spec fill; Overall body DoF per Humanoid.guide spec table; not stated on Figure AI's own pages..

hands.description: Redesigned hands with softer, more adaptive fingertips, an embedded wide-field palm camera in each hand, and first-generation fingertip tactile sensors that Figure says detect forces as small as about 3 grams.

items: head camera system with twice the frame rate, one-quarter the latency and 60% wider field of view per camera vs Figure 02 (company claim)
onboard stereo cameras used by the updated whole-body controller (reported for the ladder demo)

compute.description: Onboard compute was not specified. Figure says the robot is built for its Helix vision-language-action model and has 10 Gbps mmWave data offload for fleet learning.

actuators.description: Figure claims actuators run at 2x faster speeds with improved torque density compared with the prior generation. Electric drive per product page.

availability.notes: No public price, pre-order or retail channel was found. TIME reported at launch that the robot was not ready for domestic use.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Company demos show Figure 03 with Helix 02 unloading and reloading a dishwasher, extracting pills, dispensing syringe volumes and singulating small objects; the public package-sorting livestream showed sustained pick-and-place of small packages with barcode orientation. Hands add tactile fingertips and palm cameras.
caveats: No independent dexterity benchmark or published success rates for the fine-manipulation demos.
Dropped packages were visible during the livestream.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Figure reports a 200-hour livestreamed package-sorting run with 249,560 packages and claims no teleoperation; Helix 2.5 reports 56% zero-shot success across three household behaviors in 30 unseen homes. Helix 02 demos are described by Figure as fully autonomous.
caveats: Autonomy is company-asserted; no intervention counts or independent audit.
The 56% home success rate implies frequent failure in unseen homes.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Product page lists 1.2 m/s. Demos show walking while manipulating across a kitchen and living room, pulling a cart at BMW, and an autonomous ladder climb; robots walked to wireless charging docks during the livestream.
caveats: No fall-rate, disturbance-recovery or independent mobility metric found.
Ladder climb was not independently verified.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Figure claims an upgraded camera system plus palm cameras and tactile sensing feeding a single visuomotor network; package sorting required locating barcodes; Helix 2.5 home tests used unseen objects and layouts.
caveats: No third-party perception benchmark.
An outside expert quoted by VnExpress said accuracy was not yet sufficient for large-scale logistics.

human_interaction.summary: Figure and BMW describe upgraded audio hardware for speech-to-speech communication; the product page says users can talk to, ask or delegate tasks to the robot.
caveats: No demonstrated conversational reliability or instruction-following metric found for Figure 03.

endurance_reliability.summary: Figure reports 200 continuous hours of package sorting by a rotating group of three robots with zero hardware failures, plus a 10-hour single-robot contest at 2.83 s per package versus an intern at 2.79 s. Production post reports burn-in tests and 80+ functional checks per robot.
caveats: Counts are company-reported; media relayed them without independent audit.
'Zero failures' excluded package-handling errors such as dropped or misoriented packages.
Per-robot runtime in practice was about 3-4 hours between charges.

human_environment_fit.summary: Human-sized (5'8", 61 kg) with multi-density foam at pinch points, soft textile covering and wireless foot charging; operated in Figure's internal test homes and in a BMW plant hall.
caveats: A former safety lead alleged in a disputed lawsuit that Figure robots are strong enough to cause serious injury.
No third-party safety certification of the full robot was found.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: BMW announced that Figure 03 starts a logistics sequencing use case at Plant Spartanburg; Figure says one unit is in Hall 52. Figure reports 350+ units delivered from BotQ by April 2026, allocated mostly to internal programs.
caveats: No Figure 03 output, hours or intervention metrics from BMW yet.
BMW's 30,000-vehicle metric belongs to Figure 02, not Figure 03.

accessibility_value.summary: No public price, purchase path, lease offer or waitlist was found in primary sources.
caveats: Not purchasable by the public as of the review date.

evidence_items.title: Figure 03 product-page specifications
evidence_items.claim: Figure lists Figure 03 at 5'8", 61 kg, 20 kg payload, 1.2 m/s, 5 hours runtime, electric drive.
evidence_items.notes: Official spec page; values are not independently measured.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Defines size, payload, speed and runtime for comparison.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company spec page. Runtime spec is longer than the 3-4 hour charge rotation reported during the livestream.

evidence_items.title: Figure 03 launch hardware claims
evidence_items.claim: Figure says Figure 03 adds a camera system with twice the frame rate, one-quarter the latency and 60% wider field of view per camera, palm cameras, fingertip tactile sensors detecting about 3 g, 2 kW wireless foot charging, a UN38.3-certified battery, 10 Gbps mmWave data offload, soft textile covering with multi-density foam, and 9% less mass than Figure 02.
evidence_items.notes: Official launch claims, relative to Figure 02.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Hardware basis for tactile/vision manipulation and home safety claims.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Launch post lists camera improvements, palm cameras, 3-gram fingertip sensing, 2 kW wireless charging, UN38.3 battery certification, mmWave offload and soft textiles.
evidence_items.source_location: Introducing Figure 03 post, hardware, hands, battery and home-safety sections
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company launch source; relative improvements are not independently measured.

evidence_items.title: Helix 02 dishwasher loco-manipulation demo
evidence_items.claim: Figure published video of Figure 03 unloading and reloading a dishwasher across a full-sized kitchen in a four-minute task combining walking, manipulation and balance.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Strongest long-horizon household manipulation demo for this robot.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Helix 02 post describes a four-minute end-to-end dishwasher unload/reload across a full kitchen.
evidence_items.source_location: Introducing Helix 02 post, long-horizon loco-manipulation section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company demo; playback speed, number of attempts and success rate were not disclosed.

evidence_items.title: Helix 02 autonomy and architecture claims
evidence_items.claim: Figure states the Helix 02 demo videos are fully autonomous and not teleoperated, with no resets or human intervention in the dishwasher run, and that its System 0 whole-body controller was trained on over 1,000 hours of retargeted human motion data and replaces 109,504 lines of hand-written C++.
evidence_items.notes: Internal/autonomy claims split from the observable demo.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Supports autonomy framing but cannot be checked externally.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Post says the videos are fully autonomous, not teleoperated, and describes System 0/1/2 and training data.
evidence_items.source_location: Introducing Helix 02 post, autonomy statements and System 0 section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company statement; no external audit of execution mode.

evidence_items.title: Helix 02 fine-dexterity demos
evidence_items.claim: Figure shows Figure 03 with Helix 02 extracting individual pills, dispensing a precise 5 ml syringe volume, unscrewing a bottle cap and picking small metal pieces from clutter, using tactile sensing and palm cameras.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Fine-motor evidence above most humanoid demos, but without success rates.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Helix 02 post shows pill extraction, syringe dispensing, cap unscrewing and singulation from clutter.
evidence_items.verification_notes: No trial counts or failure data; not independently replicated.

evidence_items.title: Helix 02 living room tidy demo
evidence_items.claim: Figure published a whole-body living room cleanup demo in which the robot walks through a room while manipulating objects, tools and containers.
evidence_items.notes: Page does not state duration, autonomy mode or success rate.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Post describes end-to-end living room cleanup with tool use and bimanual manipulation.
evidence_items.verification_notes: No teleoperation disclosure, timing or success data on the page.

evidence_items.title: Figure 03 production ramp
evidence_items.claim: Figure reports more than 350 Figure 03 robots delivered from BotQ, production raised from 1 per day to 1 per hour within 120 days, end-of-line first-pass yield above 80%, and 80+ functional tests per robot before sign-off.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Shows the robot exists at fleet scale; units go mostly to internal programs.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Post lists 350+ deliveries, 1 robot per hour, >80% first-pass yield, 500+ battery packs, 9,000+ actuators.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company figures; 'delivered' includes internal R&D and data-collection allocation, not external customers.

evidence_items.title: Public package-sorting livestream (observable)
evidence_items.claim: Figure livestreamed Figure 03 robots at its headquarters picking small packages, finding barcodes and placing them barcode-down on a conveyor around the clock, rotating robots to recharge; viewers could see occasional mistakes such as dropped packages.
evidence_items.notes: Unusually transparent: continuous public video rather than an edited clip.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Strong observable evidence for repetitive logistics work over long durations.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Media describe a continuous public stream of robots sorting packages, robot rotation for charging, and visible dropped packages.
evidence_items.source_location: Startup Fortune, Ars Technica republish and Interesting Engineering livestream reports
evidence_items.verification_notes: Reviewed via media descriptions, not by watching the stream. Controlled company environment; hidden assistance cannot be ruled out by outside observers.

evidence_items.title: Livestream final tally (company-reported)
evidence_items.claim: Figure reported that the livestream ran 200 hours over nine days with three rotating Figure 03 robots sorting 249,560 packages, with zero hardware failures and no humans in the loop.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Sherwood and Interesting Engineering report 200 hours, 249,560 packages and no robot failures, citing Figure/Adcock.
evidence_items.source_location: Sherwood News and Interesting Engineering 200-hour reports
evidence_items.verification_notes: Counts not independently audited. Interesting Engineering notes 'failures' excluded dropped or misoriented packages.

evidence_items.title: 10-hour human vs robot sorting contest
evidence_items.claim: In a 10-hour livestreamed contest, an intern sorted 12,924 packages at 2.79 s each versus about 12,732 packages at 2.83 s each for the Figure 03 robot side.
evidence_items.notes: Sherwood reports 12,735 robot packages; VnExpress and the Ars republish report 12,732.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Near-human throughput on one simple repetitive task.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Intern 12,924 packages at 2.79 s; robot about 12,732 at 2.83 s over 10 hours, announced by Adcock.
evidence_items.source_location: VnExpress contest article; Ars Technica republish; Sherwood News
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company-announced result; human was given breaks; accuracy of each side not published.

evidence_items.title: Media cautions on the livestream
evidence_items.claim: Coverage notes no published intervention counts, failure rates or uptime logs, no independent verification, and an Ohio State expert said the robots lacked the accuracy needed for large-scale logistics.
evidence_items.notes: Caution item to temper livestream credit.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Limits how far livestream numbers should push autonomy and reliability scores.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Startup Fortune and Fox call the run company evidence, not independent evidence; VnExpress quotes Ayanna Howard on accuracy.
evidence_items.source_location: Startup Fortune critical-gaps section; Fox News caveats; VnExpress expert quote

evidence_items.title: BMW announces Figure 03 sequencing use case
evidence_items.claim: BMW Group says Figure 03 will start at Plant Spartanburg on logistics sequencing, picking unsorted components from containers and sorting them into sequencing trolleys for just-in-sequence delivery to assembly.
evidence_items.notes: Customer-confirmed task, but no hours, output or unit counts; therefore capped below Tier 4.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Customer validation that Figure 03 is entering a production environment.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: BMW release describes the sequencing task and Figure 03 features; Figure 02 results are cited as precedent.
evidence_items.source_location: BMW Group press release 2026-06-25, Spartanburg Figure 03 project
evidence_items.verification_notes: Customer source. Release headline says Figure AI 'demonstrates' Figure 03 in a new use case and robot development runs in parallel, so treat as early-stage.

evidence_items.title: F.03 at BMW Hall 52 demo
evidence_items.claim: Figure shows one Figure 03 at BMW Spartanburg Hall 52 grasping parts that arrive in variable orientations with both hands while stepping and repositioning to pull a heavy cart on casters, controlled by Helix 02.
evidence_items.notes: No cycle time, success rate or hours published.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Shows the industrial task visually; whole-body loco-manipulation in a real plant.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Figure post describes parts sequencing plus cart pulling with dynamic whole-body control.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company post; single unit; no performance data.

evidence_items.title: Autonomous ladder climb demo
evidence_items.claim: Figure posted video of Figure 03 climbing a ladder, saying it was fully autonomous using an updated Helix whole-body controller trained with reinforcement learning in simulation and using onboard stereo cameras.
evidence_items.notes: Single clip posted on X by the CEO, reviewed via media report.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Unusual whole-body mobility skill for a humanoid.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Interesting Engineering describes the ladder ascent and Figure's autonomy and sim-to-real claims.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Article notes the demo was not independently verified and technical details were not disclosed.

evidence_items.title: Helix 2.5 zero-shot home generalization
evidence_items.claim: Figure reports that its Index-pretrained Helix 2.5 policy succeeded 56% of the time (vs 9% without pretraining) on living-room tidying, towel folding and bed making in 30 Bay Area homes where no data had been collected.
evidence_items.notes: Company-run evaluation with a published success rate; trial counts per home not given.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Rare quantified home-generalization result, including a substantial failure rate.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Post reports 56% zero-shot success across three whole-body behaviors in 30 unseen homes.
evidence_items.source_location: Helix 2.5: Zero-Shot 30-Home Generalization post, results section
evidence_items.verification_notes: Company evaluation; not peer-reviewed or replicated; per-task breakdown not published.

evidence_items.title: Launch-time readiness for homes
evidence_items.claim: TIME reported at launch that Figure 03 was not ready for domestic use, with initial deployment to select partners; Adcock said all-day autonomy was not there yet and targeted 2026.
evidence_items.notes: TIME's in-person observations of failures concerned Figure 02 and are not credited against Figure 03.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: TIME: not ready for domestic use; Adcock: 'We're not there yet. We think we can get there in 2026.'

evidence_items.title: Whistleblower safety lawsuit
evidence_items.claim: Figure's former head of product safety sued, alleging Figure humanoids are powerful enough to fracture a human skull and that a malfunctioning robot gashed a steel refrigerator door; Figure denies the claims.
evidence_items.notes: Allegations are disputed and not tied to a specific model in the reviewed report.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Safety caution for home and human-proximity scenarios.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Lawsuit alleges skull-fracturing force and gutted safety roadmap; Figure says the plaintiff was fired for poor performance.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Unproven allegations in litigation; do not treat as established fact.

evidence_items.title: Height conflict
evidence_items.claim: Figure's product page lists 5'8" while TIME's launch article says 5-foot-6.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Minor; does not change human-environment fit.
evidence_items.source_location: Product page spec strip; TIME article body
evidence_items.verification_notes: Two-inch discrepancy; product page treated as canonical.

evidence_items.title: Missing disclosures
evidence_items.claim: No total DoF, hand DoF, battery capacity, price, intervention rate, failure rate per task, BMW output metrics or independent benchmark were found for Figure 03.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Judges should reduce confidence on autonomy and value.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Gaps identified across all reviewed primary and secondary sources.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Absence of disclosure, not evidence of inability.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Figure 03 has the strongest public long-duration task evidence of any Figure robot (a 200-hour livestreamed package-sorting run) and a customer-confirmed BMW use case, but most numbers are company-reported and BMW has not yet published Figure 03 output metrics.
strongest_positive_evidence: Continuous public livestream of package sorting with company-reported 200 hours and 249,560 packages.
10-hour contest at 2.83 s per package vs 2.79 s for a human.
BMW customer release confirming a Figure 03 logistics sequencing task.
Helix 02 long-horizon household and fine-dexterity demos; Helix 2.5 56% zero-shot success in 30 homes.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No independent benchmark or intervention log.
No BMW output or hours for Figure 03.
No DoF, battery capacity or compute disclosure.
conflicting_claims: Robot packages in 10-hour contest: 12,732 (VnExpress, Ars republish) vs 12,735 (Sherwood).
Runtime: 5 hours on spec page vs 3-4 hour charge rotation reported during livestream.
Fan-run trackers published interim totals that differ from Figure's final tally; Figure's tally used.
do_not_overclaim: Do not credit Figure 02's BMW metrics (30,000+ X3 vehicles, 1,250 hours) to Figure 03.
Do not describe Figure 03 as purchasable or home-deployed to consumers.
Do not treat livestream counts as independently audited.
Do not read 'zero failures' as zero handling errors.

currentness.currentness_notes: Figure 03 is Figure's current production humanoid as of 2026-10-17. Sherwood News reported in May 2026 that the Figure 04 design was finalized, but no Figure 04 release was found.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Figure 03 is Figure AI's current third-generation biped humanoid (5'8", 61 kg, 20 kg payload, 5 h listed runtime, 1.2 m/s) with tactile fingertips, palm cameras and wireless foot charging. Its strongest evidence is a public package-sorting livestream that Figure reports ran 200 hours with 249,560 packages and near-human per-package speed, plus a BMW-confirmed logistics sequencing use case at Spartanburg. Household and dexterity demos (dishwasher, pills, syringe, 56% zero-shot success in 30 homes) are company-published. Autonomy is asserted but not independently audited, BMW has published no Figure 03 output metrics, and the robot is not for sale.
strongest_evidence: 10-hour contest: 2.83 s per package vs 2.79 s for a human (figure-03_evidence_010).
BMW customer release confirming Figure 03 sequencing task (figure-03_evidence_012).
Helix 2.5 56% zero-shot success in 30 unseen homes (figure-03_evidence_015).
weakest_evidence: No independent benchmark, intervention log or failure rate.
No BMW hours or output for Figure 03.
No price, DoF or battery capacity.
known_do_not_credit: Zero handling errors during the livestream.
